html:
The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland was the state formed in 1801, when the Act of Union joined the Kingdom of Great Britain with the Kingdom of Ireland. It lasted until most of Ireland left in 1922. On the map it appears from 1815 to 1930.

These were the years of Britain's greatest power. It was the first country of the industrial revolution, it ruled the largest empire in history, and its navy and banks set the terms of world trade. Queen Victoria reigned for 63 of its 121 years. It abolished slavery in its colonies in 1833 and slowly widened the vote at home.

Ireland was the weak joint. The Great Famine of the 1840s killed about a million people and drove another million abroad. Irish members of parliament pressed for home rule for decades. After the Easter Rising of 1916 and a war of independence, the Irish Free State was set up in 1922. The rest took the name United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland in 1927. Its longer story is under England, then Britain.
